candidates: When embedding inline icon or SVG data in test fixtures (e.g., static icon packs in `cypress/platform/viewer.js`), verify the asset has a clearly permissive license (e.g., MIT) and include the required license text directly in the file alongside the data. Also check for potential trademark restrictions that exist independently of the copyright license.
Every Mermaid diagram code block in documentation must include the diagram-type specifier (e.g., `flowchart TD`) as its first line; omitting it produces an invalid, non-renderable example.

When documentation examples reference an icon pack, use an icon that is already registered in the deployed website's Mermaid configuration (see `packages/mermaid/src/docs/.vitepress/theme/Mermaid.vue`), or update that configuration so the example renders correctly on the live site.

When adding documentation, consolidate closely related content (e.g., a syntax code block and its parameter descriptions) into a single cohesive section rather than spreading them across separate, disconnected blocks.

When existing documentation already covers a concept (e.g., `mermaid.registerIconPacks()` is documented on the architecture page), reference that canonical page with a link rather than reproducing the same information in a new file.

Any new documentation file added under `packages/mermaid/src/docs/` must be reachable from the site: either integrate it into the most relevant existing page (e.g., `packages/mermaid/src/docs/syntax/flowchart.md`) or add it to the sidebar configuration and link to it from related pages. Orphaned files that are never linked will not appear on the website.

In test setup files such as `cypress/platform/viewer.js`, define static fixture data (e.g., inline icon packs) immediately before the code that first consumes it, rather than placing it elsewhere in the file.
